subject: Finwise load test coordination - k6/Locust & SLO confirmation
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Turner <ben.turner@finwise.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 15:10:00 -0000
Subject: Recap + next steps: Finwise performance SLOs and customer-led load test

Hi Ben — thanks again for today's discovery call. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we're aligned: 

- Target SLOs you mentioned: p95 latency <= 300ms for streaming responses, sustained throughput target 200 req/s, expected concurrency ~50 concurrent streams.
- Primary scenarios to test: 1) single-stream low-latency interactive (streaming token delivery), 2) burst throughput (concurrent non-streaming requests), 3) long-context generation (KV-cache stress).
- Customer will run the load tests (your infra) and Redwood will provide test accounts, a short Locust/k6 script, and IPs to allowlist.

Proposed next steps:
1) We attach a first-pass k6 and Locust script (see attachments). Please sanity-check and tell us if you need any changes to payloads or headers.
2) We will provision a test API key with a scoped project and dataset — ETA 24 hrs after you confirm the test window.
3) Please provide the preferred 2-hour test window (we recommend weekday 10–12 PT or 18–20 PT) and a public IP range for allowlisting (or open a ticket with your firewall team).
4) Share who will be monitoring metrics on your side (name + email) so we loop them in.

I'll cc Aditya (solutions) for the script details and Rishi for commercial/discount follow-ups if the tests look good.

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Exec | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai
From: Ben Turner <ben.turner@finwise.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@finwise.com>, security@finwise.com
Date: Fri, 27 Feb 2026 09:22:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Recap + next steps: Finwise performance SLOs and customer-led load test

Thanks Marissa — clear recap, appreciated. A few clarifications from our side: 

- The 200 req/s is per-region (we'll run against your us-west cluster). Peak concurrency could spike to ~80 for short bursts; sustained concurrency expected ~50.
- Streaming behavior: we need token-at-a-time streaming for the interactive flow (clients render tokens). p95 <= 300ms is our goal for per-token latency, not end-to-end completion.
- Long-context scenario: we will send sequences up to 8k tokens to validate KV cache behavior.

We can run the test on Tuesday 3/2 between 10–12 PT. Please provision the test key and send the exact IPs to allowlist. Our infra contact for the run is Alicia Gomez (alicia.gomez@finwise.com) — she will monitor and has access to the firewall.

Also forwarding to security (security@finwise.com) for the allowlist process.

Ben
Senior Eng Manager, Platform
Ben Turner
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Turner <ben.turner@finwise.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 27 Feb 2026 12:05:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Recap + next steps: Finwise performance SLOs and customer-led load test

Thanks Ben — great, locking Tuesday 2026-03-02 10:00–12:00 PT for the initial run. A few technical notes and what I'll provide before the window: 

- Test artifacts attached: locust-script-v1.py (concurrent streaming + non-streaming scenarios) and k6-script.json (load profile for sustained throughput). The scripts have configurable variables at the top: TARGET_URL, API_KEY, CONCURRENCY, RPS, STREAMING_MODE.
- For streaming token-at-a-time we emulate chunked responses in Locust using the streaming client helper — this will exercise Redwood's streaming path.
- Suggested ramp: 0 -> 50 concurrent over 10m, hold 50 for 20m, spike to 80 for 10m, then cool down — that will surface batching/latency behavior.
- We'll create a test API key scoped to the "finwise-load-test" project and limit to 100k tokens for safety. Key will be sent via our secure vault and I'll post the vault link to you.
- IP allowlist: here are the IPs you'll need to add on your side: 34.199.12.45, 52.41.210.7, 18.205.90.33 (these are Redwood egress nodes for the us-west test cluster). If you have a CIDR preference we'll provide ranges.

Metrics we'll collect on our side: per-token p50/p95 latency, per-request end-to-end latency, throughput (req/s), GPU utilization, and queue length. Please confirm which metrics you can provide from your side (Alicia).

Attaching initial scripts. If you want we can do a short smoke run on Monday 3/1 to validate connectivity.

aroundAditya
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.ai
